NCCA Winter T20 Standing Rules (10/26/2026) Preamble
● References in this document to NCCA mean NCCA Cricket, Inc.; references to the Board or Board of Directors (BOD) mean the Board of Directors of NCCA; and references to the Executive Committee mean the Executive Officers of NCCA. NCCA is governed by its Constitution.
● Throughout this document, pronouns indicating the male gender are used purely for brevity.
● All games played under NCCA jurisdiction shall be governed by the latest ICC Men’s T20 International Playing Conditions in effect before the start of the season, except as provided in these Standing Rules. The applicable Playing Conditions shall not change during the season.
● The latest Standing Rules and approved changes posted on the NCCA website are official. The applicable edition of the ICC Men’s T20 International Playing Conditions shall be posted before the start of the season.
● The Standing Rules for a specific overs format supersede the MCC Laws of Cricket and ICC regulations for that format.
● Standing Rules are internal league regulations (Playing Conditions) for teams to follow. They are not bylaws and do not override the Constitution.
● Standing Rules supersede any other NCCA document with the exception of Constitution, if there is a conflict or ambiguity.
● This document applies exclusively to the winter league. It shall not be combined with, or interpreted by cross-reference to, the summer league rules. Page | 2

[Page 3]
NCCA Winter T20 Standing Rules (10/26/2026) 1. League Season
1.1. The NCCA Winter season shall commence no later than the second weekend of November each year.
1.2. NCCA Winter league games shall not be scheduled on the following holiday weekends. However, if the home, visiting and umpiring teams agree on a time to play during one of these weekends, they may request approval from the Match Secretaries at the start of the season.
1.2.1. Thanksgiving Weekend
1.2.2. Christmas Weekend
1.2.3. New Year’s Weekend
1.2.4. MLK Weekend
1.2.5. Presidents Day Weekend
1.3. Teams shall be scheduled to play more than one NCCA Winter game per weekend at their request.
1.4. A Club with two or more teams may, by request to the Match Secretaries, prior to the scheduling meeting, ask that at least one team from that Club be scheduled to play a game on Saturday and one on Sunday of the league weekend, and the Executive Committee shall honor all such requests subject to ground availability. 2. League Structure
2.1. NCCA winter league competitions shall use pink balls with white clothing and/or white balls with colored clothing.
2.2. The NCCA winter league competition shall be contested in divisions determined before the start of the season. Each division shall consist of no more than 13 teams.
2.2.1. The League Season shall consist of 10 to 12 games, with each team playing each other team in their division at least once and at most twice. If two teams play each other twice, they shall do so on a home-and-away basis. If a schedule is not feasible for the number of teams in the division, Match Secretaries may propose an alternative solution.
2.2.2. Division standings shall be determined according to the points accumulated by each team. In the case of a tie on points, teams shall be placed according to their Net Run Rate.
2.2.3. At the end of each season, the top 30% of the teams rounded to the nearest whole number in each of the lower divisions shall be promoted to the next higher division.
2.2.4. The bottom 30% of teams in each higher division, rounded to the nearest whole number, shall be relegated to the next lower division. Teams tied on points shall be placed according to their Net Run Rate.
2.2.5. New teams shall be placed at the bottom of the lowest division. Page | 3

[Page 4]
NCCA Winter T20 Standing Rules (10/26/2026)
2.2.6. A minimum of 7 teams is required to form a pink-ball or white-ball division.
2.3. The pink-ball competition with white clothing and the white-ball competition with colored clothing shall each be treated as a separate league, with separate playoffs.
2.4. New Teams
2.4.1. Admission of new teams to League Competition shall be by approval of the Board of Directors, and only between league seasons. New clubs must provide (or procure from existing clubs) a home ground that meets league standards. The Grounds Committee shall certify new grounds and submit the certification in writing to the Executive Committee 10 days before the start of the season in the year in which the application is made. If a new team that joins the League is sharing a ground with other teams, they must do so such that no more than 10 other teams share their home ground and the ground is available both Saturdays and Sundays. New teams shall be automatically placed on probation for their first season in the league. At the end of the probationary period, the Board of Directors, at the next General Body Meeting, shall review the facilities, standard of play and conduct of the team and approve its admission as a full member or rescind admission to the league.
2.4.2. If at least 11 players who played for a particular Team in a given season choose to leave and form or join a separate Club for the next season, they may do so (but only after the conclusion of the then-current season) while retaining their then-existing Team's Divisional (if any divisions applicable) position solely at the discretion of the Board and with the prior written approval of the Club they are departing (which former Club would thus be yielding its divisional position to the Team consisting of the departed players). The former Club shall not unreasonably withhold its approval. The NCCA shall defer to the Club management's decisions prior to the conclusion of the then-current season and may defer to the Club management's decisions thereafter. The Board shall address any controversy concerning this rule no later than the deadline for submission of Applications for the given season.
2.5. Existing Teams
2.5.1. All existing teams must continue to maintain all league standards. If a team fails to meet league standards, the Board may elect to place it on probation, suspend it, or expel it from the league immediately. If a team is expelled or has withdrawn for any reason during a season, all games it has already played and games yet to be played are treated the same as for a team that is disqualified due to a forfeit (see section 5.3). An expelled team, or a team that has withdrawn for any reason, may re-apply to join the league in future years in which event it will have to start at the lowest division and will be treated as a new team (see Section 2.4.1).
2.6. Applications and Schedule Deadlines
2.6.1. All existing and new NCCA member teams shall submit their applications, along with their dues, for the upcoming League Season by the deadline provided by NCCA Executives. Page | 4

[Page 5]
NCCA Winter T20 Standing Rules (10/26/2026)
2.6.2. All teams may provide their team’s unavailability and ground unavailability dates to the Match Secretaries during registration applications. To be eligible to compete in the NCCA league season, a team must be available to play all weekends of the whole NCCA League season, excluding weekends designated as League-wide bye weekends and Match Secretaries may try to accommodate the constraints if possible.
2.6.3. The NCCA Match Secretaries shall announce the season schedule 10 days before the first game of the season. 3. Provisions for the Game/Conditions of Play
3.1. Start Time
3.1.1. Play shall commence at the scheduled start time as per schedule uploaded on NCCA Web Portal. Requests for an exception to this rule shall be submitted to the Match Secretaries , in writing along with the applications. Such exceptions, if reasonable, shall be included in the schedule. Exceptions shall be granted on a limited basis and only to clubs that provide written documentation from the ground owner stating why the cricket facilities are not available at certain timings.
3.1.2. All league games shall consist of one innings per side. An innings shall end when the team is dismissed or its maximum allocation of twenty (20) overs is completed, whichever occurs first.
3.2. In an uninterrupted game:
3.2.1. The length of innings and minimum over rate are covered in Sections
4.2.1 and 4.2.2, respectively.
3.3. In matches where the start is delayed, or play is suspended by natural causes or force majeure :
3.3.1. The objective shall always be to rearrange the number of overs so that both teams shall have the opportunity of batting for the same number of overs. A minimum of 5 overs shall constitute a game.
3.3.2. If, owing to a suspension of play during the innings of the team batting second, it is not possible for that team to have the opportunity of batting for the same number of overs as the team batting first, they will bat for a number of overs to be calculated under the ICC Men’s T20 International Playing Conditions incorporated by the Preamble and Section
4.1. In this case, if the team batting second has neither been all out nor passed their opponent’s score, the following shall apply.
3.3.2.1. If the match is abandoned after the side batting second has faced at least 5 overs, the result shall be decided using the latest approved ICC DLS method for the par score, in accordance with ICC rules. The DLS par score shall be determined using the approved methodology on the NCCA website or scoring platform. Page | 5

[Page 6]
NCCA Winter T20 Standing Rules (10/26/2026)
3.3.2.2. If a suspension of play requires the number of overs in the second innings to be revised, the target score shall be calculated using the latest approved ICC DLS method.
3.3.2.3. Matches in which one or both teams have not had an opportunity to bat for a minimum of 5 overs shall be declared “NO RESULT” matches and points shall be awarded in accordance with Section
7.1.5.
3.3.2.4. Unless explicitly agreed between the umpires and the team captains, any game played without lights shall end by sunset time for the ground (refer to www.timeanddate.com). Refer to
3.3.2.2 for shortened games.
3.4. Delayed Start
3.4.1. All league matches shall start at the time designated unless both captains agree to a change of starting time at least twenty-four (24) hours prior to the game. It shall be the responsibility of the home team’s captain to notify the umpires, opposition team and match secretaries.
3.4.2. Automatic penalties for late start of a match shall be applied as described in Section
8.1.
3.5. Intervals
3.5.1. Innings Break . Unless otherwise agreed by the captains, the interval between innings shall not exceed 10 minutes.
3.5.2. Drinks Break . Either side may elect to take one on-field drinks interval at the halfway point of the stipulated overs.
3.5.2.1. The option of an on-field drinks interval shall be elected before the game begins.
3.5.2.2. Drinks intervals shall not exceed 5 minutes.
3.5.2.3. The agreed times for intervals shall be strictly adhered to except that if a wicket falls within one over of the agreed time, then the drinks interval shall be taken immediately.
3.5.2.4. The umpires may allow drinks to be consumed during play, providing they believe it will not waste time or delay the game.
3.5.2.5. At any time during the match, the captains may agree to forgo a drinks interval. An interval that has been forgone may be reinstated only by agreement of both captains.
3.6. Ground Conditions
3.6.1. The laying of an acceptable playing surface shall be required. It shall comply with the standards set by the Grounds Committee.
3.6.2. The captain’s report consisting of ground and umpire ratings must be completed and submitted via the scoring platform by the Wednesday following the league game. If the visiting team fails to send a report within this time, the ground shall be considered adequate by default. The Grounds Page | 6

[Page 7]
NCCA Winter T20 Standing Rules (10/26/2026) Committee will make a judgment based on the ground rating sent in by both umpires and visiting captains as to whether the ground is substandard, including judgment of whether the rating is accurate or not. Benefit of doubt shall be given to the host team when appropriate.
3.6.3. In the event that a team’s ground is judged to be substandard by the Grounds Committee, the problem areas will be identified, and the team shall be given a specified time frame in which to improve ground conditions. In the event that a team fails to comply with the recommendations of the committee, the team shall be penalized as specified in Section
8.5 for every game scheduled to be played at that ground for the period it is substandard. In addition, visiting teams shall have the option to require that any fixtures scheduled to be played at the substandard ground shall be played instead at the visiting team’s home ground. In this case, all costs for ground rental, lunch, drinks, etc. are to be paid by the original home team. If the visiting team wishes to exercise this option, it must give the home and umpiring teams, as well as the Match Secretaries and the Umpiring Committee, at least 3 days’ notice of their intention to move the venue of the fixture.
3.6.4. If the home team’s ground is unavailable on the day of play after the players and umpires arrive, the home team is responsible for paying the umpire.
3.6.5. The minimum boundary distance for NCCA games should be 60 yards where the ground dimensions permit.
3.6.6. The maximum boundary distance for NCCA games shall be 80 yards.
3.6.7. Boundary distances shall be measured from the center of the pitch.
3.6.8. Boundary sizes shall be enforced by the umpires and the umpire’s decision will be considered final and binding. The home team is responsible for providing a tape measure to verify the boundary dimensions and in the absence of a tape measure, umpires may use other alternate methods to measure.
3.7. Provisions for the Game
3.7.1. Uniform . In all League, Cup and representative games, the wearing of uniforms as approved by NCCA is required. Each player must wear the exact same uniform as the rest of the team.
3.7.1.1. For white-ball cricket, the team uniform must consist of a colored (non-white) shirt and colored trousers. Colors close to white, such as light silver or very light grey, are not allowed.
3.7.1.2. For pink-ball cricket, the team uniform must consist of a white shirt and white trousers. Colors close to red are not allowed. Colored pads are allowed provided their color is not close to red or pink.
3.7.1.3. The NCCA logo must appear on the chest of the shirt, preferably on the left side.
3.7.1.4. Logos of other leagues must not be visible.
3.7.1.5. Sponsor logos are allowed on the sleeves or back of the shirt.
3.7.1.6. Slight variations in uniform color due to fading or differences between vendors are allowed. Page | 7

[Page 8]
NCCA Winter T20 Standing Rules (10/26/2026)
3.7.2. Footwear . No batter or bowler shall be permitted to wear footwear that has hard studs, spikes or cleats unless the game is played on a natural turf wicket and as permitted by the ground custodian.
3.7.3. Protective Equipment . Leg Guards (pads) shall be of approximately the same color as the predominant color in the uniform. All protective equipment except leg-guards, gloves, arm guards and helmets should be worn underneath the player’s clothing. Thigh guards, abdomen guards, chest guards etc. should not be worn on top of the shirt or pants. (Refer to section
3.7.1 for uniform provisions.)
3.7.3.1. Helmet . A helmet is mandatory for a batter facing a seam-up bowler and for a wicketkeeper standing up to the stumps, regardless of the bowler’s pace. A helmet is also mandatory for fielders, other than those at slip, gully or fine leg, standing within eight (8) yards of the striker’s end. Batters must wear helmets except when facing slow bowlers.
3.7.4. Penalty . Any player in contravention of the Rules in Sections
3.7.1 and
3.7.3 will be subject to a penalty as described in Section
8.7.
3.7.5. Ball . Each fielding team shall have one new ball for its innings, to be used from both ends.
3.7.5.1. All league and playoff games shall use NCAA-approved T20 white or pink balls supplied by NCCA. No other brand or type of ball is allowed unless approved in writing by the Match Secretaries.
3.7.5.2. The home team shall provide spare balls to be used if the game ball is lost.
3.7.6. Other Provisions . The home team shall provide a first aid kit and adequate seating for the teams / spectators.
3.7.7. Ground . If the home team’s ground is unavailable for a league game, an available league-approved ground may be used as an alternative.
3.7.7.1. It is the responsibility of the home team to obtain a league-approved ground for that league game.
3.7.7.2. The home team must give the visiting and umpiring teams at least 2 days’ notice of a venue change and communicate the exact venue at least 24 hours before the scheduled start.
3.7.8. Umpires . The umpires shall wear NCCA approved Colored Umpiring Clothing (or White/light colored clothing for Pink ball division) and dark colored trousers. Failure to do so will be penalized as described in Section
8.4. Page | 8

[Page 9]
NCCA Winter T20 Standing Rules (10/26/2026)
3.8. Rescheduling Games
3.8.1. If a majority of league games on a weekend are abandoned or canceled due to natural causes or force majeure, the Match Secretaries may, at their discretion, reschedule those games on a subsequent weekend.
3.8.2. A home team proposing a venue change must select an NCCA-approved ground for that division within 45 miles’ driving distance of the originally scheduled ground. The home team should notify the visiting team, umpiring team and Match Secretaries by the end of Thursday. Objections will not be considered after noon on Friday. The Match Secretaries must approve the change by 6 p.m. on Friday. Once the game is played, the result stands.
3.8.3. The Match Secretaries may approve a change of date and venue by Wednesday, provided the new date is at least one week away from the originally scheduled date. All parties involved must agree to the change, and the Match Secretaries must approve it. The rescheduled game should take place before the last game of the season for that group in that division.
3.8.4. Games cannot be rescheduled due to selection of some members of a team for representative games.
3.8.5. The Match Secretaries may reschedule games that conflict with an NCCA-hosted event. 4. Laws of the Game
4.1. NCCA follows the applicable ICC Men’s T20 Playing Conditions posted on the NCCA website. Changes shall not be implemented during the season.
4.2. Exceptions to ICC Men’s T20 International Playing Conditions
4.2.1. Length of Innings
4.2.1.1. Uninterrupted Matches . Each team shall bat for 20 overs unless all out earlier.
4.2.2. Minimum Over Rate
4.2.2.1. The minimum over rate shall be
13.33 overs per hour, equivalent to
4.5 minutes per over. A maximum of 90 minutes of playing time is allowed for 20 overs, excluding drinks breaks and the time allowances listed in Section
4.2.2.2.
4.2.2.2. Allowance shall be given for drinks breaks, injuries, lost balls or other circumstances beyond the control of the fielding team.
4.2.2.3. For the purpose of calculating the over rate, if an over has been started by the scheduled time of cessation, it shall be considered as having been completed.
4.2.2.4. If the team fielding first fails to bowl the required number of overs by the scheduled time for cessation of the first innings, play shall continue until the required number of overs Page | 9

[Page 10]
NCCA Winter T20 Standing Rules (10/26/2026) has been bowled. The team batting second shall receive its full quota of overs irrespective of the number of overs it bowled in the scheduled time for the cessation of the first innings.
4.2.2.5. If the team batting first is dismissed in less than its allotted number of overs, the team batting second shall be entitled to bat for its full allotment of overs.
4.2.2.6. If the team fielding second fails to bowl its allotted number of overs by the scheduled cessation time, the hours of play shall be extended until the required number of overs has been bowled or a result is achieved.
4.2.2.7. Penalties shall apply to either team (or both teams, if applicable) for slow over rates. See Section
4.2.3 for definition of offenses and Section
8.8 for penalties.
4.2.3. Minimum Over Rate Offenses . Failure by a fielding team to meet the Minimum Over Rate requirements constitutes an offense by the relevant Team Captain and each of the Players in that fielding team according to the following:
4.2.3.1. Where the actual over rate is up to (and including) two overs short of the Minimum Over Rate, such an offense shall be considered a ‘Minor Over Rate Offense’. So, for a 20 over game, if 18 or 19 overs (including the over in progress) have been bowled by the scheduled cessation time, the fielding team is guilty of a "Minor Over Rate Offense".
4.2.3.2. Where the actual over rate is more than two overs short of the Minimum Over Rate, such an offense shall be considered a ‘Serious Over Rate Offense’. So, for a 20 over game, if 17 or fewer overs (including the over in progress) have been bowled by the scheduled cessation time, the fielding team is guilty of a "Serious Over Rate Offense". Note: Subjective intent on behalf of the Team Captain to waste time is not required. It is sufficient to establish that the Minimum Over Rate was not met. To avoid liability under this offense the Team Captain would need to establish, on the balance of probabilities, that the shortfall was due to factors beyond his control and that the time allowances permitted by the Match officials in calculating the required over rate were not sufficient. The scoring platform tracks timings for each over which can be used to make any judgments about where delays were.
4.2.4. No Ball . For all matches played on pitches other than natural grass the following additions to Law 21.7-No Ball shall apply:
4.2.4.1. Either Umpire shall call and signal "No Ball," when a ball delivered by the bowler pitches on the bound edge of the matting or other material used as a playing surface, on a fastening string or strap or on any spike or other device used to secure the playing surface whether it be on the playing surface or not, or it pitches in a hole or area of disrepair within the playing surface whether the edges are bound or not. Page | 10

[Page 11]
NCCA Winter T20 Standing Rules (10/26/2026)
4.2.4.2. Either umpire shall call and signal “No Ball” when a delivery pitches on an edge or seam of a repaired part of the playing surface and bounces unusually in a way that, in the umpire’s opinion, was caused by that edge or seam.
4.2.4.3. The ball shall not become dead when an event described in Section
4.2.4.1 or
4.2.4.2 occurs. It remains in play, and either batter may be dismissed only in a manner permitted following a No Ball.
4.2.4.4. A delivery called “No Ball” shall not also be called “Wide Ball”; No Ball takes precedence.
4.2.4.5. If the ball comes to rest in front of the line of Striker’s wicket, without having previously been touched by the bat or person of the striker, the umpire shall call “No Ball” and immediately “Dead Ball” so that no further actions (runs or wickets) can happen from that delivery. 5. General Rules
5.1. Players
5.1.1. Player Registration
5.1.1.1. Before the first game of the league season a club must register at least eleven players per team, along with email addresses, if available.
5.1.1.2. Players must be registered on the scoring platform as a player for the Club for which they intend to play and then selected for a specific team under that club. This registration must include full first and last name and a recent photograph of the player. Short names, nicknames or initials are not allowed. If, during approval of the scorecard, Match Secretaries find that these requirements have not been met for any player, they have the authority to penalize teams per Section
8.6.1.
5.1.1.3. All players in any league game must be registered with the club for which they play. New players must be registered with the team before being eligible to play for the team. If the team fields a player that has not been registered with the team prior to the game being played, then the team will be penalized 10 points.
5.1.1.4. All players participating in NCCA-sanctioned events or representative teams shall be registered members of NCCA. Membership shall be granted to an individual who provides the required personal demographic information (“registration information”), agrees to NCCA’s membership terms and conditions, and pays the applicable membership fee.
5.1.1.5. Each registered player shall submit a completed registration form as provided by the NCCA.
5.1.1.6. Each member shall agree to abide by the following terms and conditions: Page | 11

[Page 12]
NCCA Winter T20 Standing Rules (10/26/2026)
● Comply with corresponding NCCA Standing Rules and conduct oneself in a manner consistent with the Preamble and the Spirit of Cricket per applicable T20 playing conditions as posted on NCCA Website.
● Comply with the NCCA & ICC Code of Conduct.
● Supply accurate personal demographic information to the NCCA and notify the Association promptly of changes to this information.
● Submit and endorse the liability waiver required during registration.
● Affirm that the member is not currently banned or suspended from play by the ICC or any Association affiliated with the USA Cricket.
● Adhere to the NCCA fair play rating system and abide by decisions of the Match Secretaries, committees and/or Board concerning penalties, suspensions and terminations under that system.
5.1.2. Player Eligibility
5.1.2.1. All players may play multiple games during the same weekend.
5.1.2.2. No player who has been suspended by NCCA for disciplinary reasons will be allowed to play in league games until that player has completely served out the time of suspension in full. If the player is part of a team that disbanded during the season, the games missed do not qualify as part of the sentence.
5.1.2.3. Per the ICC rules, an Under 17 player is defined as a player who is under the age of 17 on the 1st of September prior to the season start date.
5.1.2.4. A player may play for only one team in the league unless the player transfers under Section 5.1.3, subject to the U17 exception in Section
5.1.2.5.
5.1.2.5. U17 players may play for 2 teams within the same club.
5.1.2.6. A player can play a maximum of 14 regular season games prior to playoffs. U17 players are exempt from this rule.
5.1.2.7. A player must have played at least 2 matches for a team during the season to be eligible to play for that team in the playoffs, subject to the professional-player requirements in Section
5.1.2.11.
5.1.2.8. Any violations of player eligibility rules noted or brought to the attention of and confirmed by the Match Secretaries will result in the offending team being deemed to have forfeited the game(s) in question.
5.1.2.9. A player cannot participate in the match without a NCCA approved team uniform. All the players of a team must have a matching uniform.
5.1.2.10. A professional league player (“pro player”) is defined as a player who has: Page | 12

[Page 13]
NCCA Winter T20 Standing Rules (10/26/2026)
5.1.2.10.1. Represented a nation, or been included in its squad, in an ICC-recognized international cricket competition, excluding under-19 and under-17 competitions.
5.1.2.10.2. Played in the domestic cricket circuit in any ICC full member or associate nation ( for example, Ranji trophy/ County Cricket, etc.)
5.1.2.10.3. Played 2 or more games in professional leagues worldwide, such as MLC, MiLC, CPL, SAT20, BBL, ILT20 or GT20.
5.1.2.10.4. A player is not considered a pro player if the player has not actively played in professional leagues in the 5 years before the start of the season.
5.1.2.10.5. A player is not considered a pro player if the player has played more NCCA-sanctioned games across all formats (excluding NCCA tournaments) than professional-league games. NCCA’s official scoring platform statistics at the start of the season shall be used to count NCCA games.
5.1.2.10.6. An O50 player is not considered a pro player even if the player has previously played in professional leagues.
5.1.2.10.7. Pro players may transfer only once per season, and the transfer must be requested during the first transfer window.
5.1.2.11. A pro player may play in a team’s last 5 games of the season only if the player has played in at least 2 of that team’s first 7 games. This rule applies to all pro players except U19 players. To be eligible for the playoffs, a pro player must have played at least 4 league games.
5.1.2.12. Pro players may play only for teams in their club’s highest division and may not play for the club’s teams in lower divisions.
5.1.2.13. Each club is responsible for determining whether a player is a pro player. If a complaint is filed and a violation of the pro-player rule is established, the Match Committee shall decide on the reported violation.
5.1.2.14. A player must be at least 13 years old on April 1 immediately before the start of the season to play in NCCA adult matches. A younger player with exceptional talent must obtain prior approval from the Match Secretaries. The Match Secretaries shall establish approval criteria and apply them uniformly to all applicants.
5.1.3. Player Transfer Between Teams Players changing teams during the season must have their release approved by their former club before they can play in the NCCA Competition for another team. Such approval shall not be unreasonably withheld and is subject to the following rules. Page | 13

[Page 14]
NCCA Winter T20 Standing Rules (10/26/2026)
5.1.3.1. A transfer request must be submitted to the Match Secretaries by the player or the player’s new team. An official of the former club should be copied on the request.
5.1.3.2. If a new team submits a transfer request on a player’s behalf, the Match Secretaries must confirm that the player is requesting the transfer.
5.1.3.3. The Match Secretaries and former club must receive the request for transfer before the end of Wednesday if the transferred player is to play for his new club the following weekend.
5.1.3.4. If no legitimate reason is provided within 48 hours by the former club for withholding the transfer, such transfer shall be considered granted.
5.1.3.5. The Match Secretaries shall determine if any reasons provided for denial of transfer are reasonable.
5.1.3.6. A player may change teams up to twice per season - once within each transfer window. The first transfer window runs from the start of the season through December 31; the second runs from January 1 through February 15. Transfer requests should be sent to the Match Secretaries within the relevant window. Pro players are subject to Section
5.1.2.10.7.
5.1.3.7. Games played before a transfer count toward the game limit in Section
5.1.2.6.
5.1.3.8. If a team is found to have fielded a player who is ineligible in accordance with these rules, it will automatically forfeit the game in question and points will be awarded in accordance with
7.1.1.
5.1.3.9. If a team disbands or is removed from the league for failing to meet its obligations, a player may join another club or team of the player’s choice. The player may not play for that club or team until it has submitted the player’s registration and the registration has been accepted.
5.2. Reporting of Results
5.2.1. Before the start of the season, the NCCA Executive Committee shall announce the official scoring platform for reporting all game results.
5.2.2. The use of the official Scoring Platform application is mandatory for all teams.
5.2.3. The home team must report the results of all league games. Failure to report results and submit the information required below on time will incur the penalties in Section
8.6.
5.2.4. Scorecard edits and the Player of the Match (PoM) selection must be entered in the scoring platform by the end of Wednesday immediately following the game. The PoM selection may not be changed after that deadline, including where no selection was entered. The Match Secretaries will consider scorecard correction requests only within two weeks after the match ends, provided both teams agree and submit a joint written request. Page | 14

[Page 15]
NCCA Winter T20 Standing Rules (10/26/2026)
5.2.5. If a manual scorecard is entered into the Scoring Platform, then the paper score sheets used for scoring must be emailed to the appropriate Match Secretary by the end of the day Wednesday immediately following the game.
5.2.6. In case of a rained-out game or forfeited game, a basic scorecard must be entered into the Scoring Platform.
5.2.7. Each team captain must fill out the Umpire's Feedback Report on the Scoring Platform by the Wednesday following the league game.
5.2.8. Umpires must verify the squads on the scoring platform and check that the teams have selected the correct umpires for the game.
5.2.9. Umpires may verify players’ identification when needed. If a player cannot be verified on the squad or through identification, the umpire shall not allow that player to play.
5.3. Forfeits
5.3.1. A team forfeiting a game during the regular league season will no longer be disqualified from all NCCA games for the season but will be assessed a fine of $250 for each forfeited game.
5.3.2. All player eligibility violations should be recorded as forfeits in the scoring platform, which will automatically calculate NRR under Section
7.2.1. However, only forfeits involving a walkover, failure to play a scheduled NCCA game or use of a suspended player shall carry a monetary penalty, payable under Section
8.9.
5.3.3. A team forfeiting a game during the playoffs will be assessed a fine of $250.
5.3.4. A team forfeiting an NCCA game shall reimburse the home team receiving the forfeit for its ground rental cost. The home team should provide a receipt from the city or booking authority showing the amount paid.
5.4. Dispute Resolution
5.4.1. In the event that disputes arise on the field, the captain(s) and/or umpire(s) must submit a written report to the Match Secretaries . Match Secretaries shall be responsible for taking appropriate action or may forward the report to the appropriate committee for action. The results of the investigation (if any) shall be forwarded in writing to the club secretary, umpires and players involved.
5.4.2. Any appeal of a decision by the Match Committees or Disciplinary Committee, by a team or a player, can only be made to the Executive Committee and such appeal must be made in writing within 48 hours of the decision being communicated to the team or player. Each appeal must also be accompanied by a deposit of $300, which will be refunded if the appeal is successful. Page | 15

[Page 16]
NCCA Winter T20 Standing Rules (10/26/2026)
5.5. Ground Protection Rule Any current or new member(s) belonging to a Club/Team in NCCA shall not approach another Club/Team's home ground, facility and/or city officials regarding facility usage for any purpose (temporary, permanent or in future) without an official communication to the NCCA club/clubs. Failure to comply with the above rule may result in any of the following:
5.5.1. Placing the individual(s) and/or associated club on probation for at least 2 years for violating the general league code of conduct.
5.5.2. Not allowing the violating member/team to use the facility for NCCA games.
5.5.3. Any additional penalty that the NCCA Board deems necessary. 6. Umpiring
6.1. Assignment of Umpires
6.1.1. A t the start of the season, the Match Secretaries shall designate non-participating (neutral) teams to provide one bowler’s-end umpire (BEU) for each match. The designated team is responsible for the umpire’s punctual attendance. The BEU should hold at least Level 3 certification. Captains may not veto a certified umpire provided by the neutral team.
6.1.2. If a team assigned to provide a neutral umpire engages an external umpire who is not a club member, the assigned team remains liable for any no-show or late-arrival penalty. Umpire fees payable by teams shall be those approved by the Board for T20 games.
6.1.3. The Umpiring Committee shall assign panel umpires from the NCCA pool to selected games, with one panel umpire per match until the pool is exhausted. The Match Secretaries shall notify both playing teams and the team assigned to provide an umpire no later than the Thursday before the game.
6.1.4. The captain of the batting side shall be responsible for appointing an umpire who shall stand as Striker’s End Umpire only.
6.1.5. In the event that the appointed neutral umpire does not attend the game, the captain of the batting side shall be responsible for the appointment of a Bowler End Umpire as well. Both Captains shall be responsible for the good conduct and completion of the game.
6.1.6. Failure to provide Umpires shall result in a point penalty and a monetary fine per umpire per game, as specified in Section
8.3. Point penalties shall apply to league games only.
6.1.7. Bowler’s-end umpires must be NCCA-certified umpires.
6.1.8. The team umpire should have played a minimum of 2 games for the most recent club. Certified parent umpires are allowed to officiate for the team on behalf of the youth player if his/her child Page | 16

[Page 17]
NCCA Winter T20 Standing Rules (10/26/2026) has played in a minimum of 2 games in the last 2 seasons. If a team sends a non-team/non-club member to umpire, the umpire shall be considered as NO SHOW & apply penalties as described in section
8.3.1.
6.2. Age Guidelines for Umpires
6.2.1. For their safety and well-being, players aged 16 or below on game day may officiate only at the striker’s end. Players below age 13 may not umpire.
6.2.2. It is the responsibility of the team that has the umpiring assignment to make sure that these age-related guidelines are strictly adhered to. All other requirements (e.g. Level 3 certification) for an umpire must still be met.
6.2.3. If a playing team encounters an umpire under 16 on game day, it may insist that the umpire officiate only at the striker’s end and that the senior umpire officiate at the bowler’s end from both ends of the pitch. If a team suspects that an umpire is under 16, it should request proof of age. 7. Points - Competition Points for all divisions
7.1. Competition Points will be awarded as follows:
7.1.1. Walkover or Forfeit = 20 points to non-forfeiting team
7.1.2. Win = 20 points
7.1.3. Loss = 0 points
7.1.4. Tie = 10 points each
7.1.5. No Result = 10 points each.
7.2. Net Run Rate (NRR)
7.2.1. Net Run Rate (NRR) is calculated automatically by the scoring platform.
7.3. The following registration-fee awards shall be made:
7.3.1. The league-table champions’ full registration fee for the next season shall be waived.
7.3.2. Half of the runners-up’s registration fee for the next season shall be waived. 8. Penalties
8.1. Automatic penalties for the late start of a match shall be as follows:
8.1.1. A team without seven players present and visible to the umpires 15 minutes before the scheduled start automatically loses the toss. If neither team has seven players present, the toss shall be delayed until one team has seven players present; that team automatically wins the toss. If both teams’ seventh players arrive simultaneously, a toss shall be conducted in the presence of an umpire. Page | 17

[Page 18]
NCCA Winter T20 Standing Rules (10/26/2026)
8.1.2. A team without seven players present at the agreed start time shall be penalized two overs. Players must be visible to the umpire from the field of play; a player in the parking lot or another location out of the umpire’s sight does not count as present. A further two-over penalty applies if the team cannot take the field with at least seven players within 15 minutes after the agreed start time.
8.1.3. If either team is still in violation of Sections
8.1.1 or
8.1.2 thirty (30) minutes after the agreed starting time, the offending team will automatically forfeit the game.
8.1.4. In the event that neither team has seven (7) players on the ground thirty (30) minutes after the official starting time, the match shall be declared null and void and zero (0) points shall be awarded.
8.1.5. The home side shall lose two (2) overs of batting time if the ground is not ready for play at the agreed start time.
8.2. Penalties for unfair play
8.2.1. The following provisions apply to all NCCA games in addition to Law 42.
8.2.1.1. In the event that either Umpire has experienced an act of Unfair Play under the NCCA Code of conduct, the Umpires shall forward a brief account of the incident to the NCCA Match Secretaries , who shall in turn forward it to the NCCA Disciplinary Committee. The report should be received within 3 days of the incident, and in any case no later than one week after the game.
8.3. Umpires Not Sent:
8.3.1. If the assigned Level 3 or higher certified umpire fails to attend a game, the assigned umpiring team shall receive a 10-point penalty and a $100 fine. Each subsequent occurrence shall incur a 10-point penalty and a $250 fine.
8.3.2. A neutral umpire arriving after the start time and up to one hour late shall incur a $100 late-arrival penalty, with no point penalty. An umpire arriving one hour after the start time shall be treated as a no-show under Section
8.3.1.
8.4. Umpire with Improper Attire:
8.4.1. Umpires must wear proper attire while officiating.
8.4.1.1. For pink-ball cricket, the BEU must wear a white shirt or T-shirt, dark-colored trousers and shoes or sneakers.
8.4.1.2. For white-ball cricket, the BEU must wear a colored shirt or T-shirt that allows the batter to see the white ball clearly, dark-colored trousers and shoes or sneakers.
8.4.1.3. Sleeveless shirts or undershirts may not be worn without a covering garment.
8.4.1.4. Shorts are not allowed. Page | 18

[Page 19]
NCCA Winter T20 Standing Rules (10/26/2026)
8.4.1.5. Flip-flops and other open-toed footwear are not allowed.
8.4.2. Teams are requested to submit photographic or video evidence of an umpire’s failure to comply with Section
8.4.1 to the Match Secretaries within 10 days. The team responsible for providing that umpire shall receive a 10-point penalty.
8.4.3. Panel umpires must also wear proper attire and are subject to appropriate penalties for noncompliance. The team originally assigned to provide an umpire shall not be penalized for a panel umpire’s attire. Teams are encouraged to submit photographic or video evidence to the Umpiring Committee and Match Secretaries.
8.5. Sub-Standard Grounds:
8.5.1. A team shall receive a five (5) point deduction and a $50 fine for each home game played on a ground designated as substandard by the Grounds Committee.
8.6. Failure to Report Results and Submit Required Information on Time.
8.6.1. A team that fails to submit a scorecard, match report or umpire rating, or to upload photographs of the opposition and umpires, by the Wednesday after the game shall be fined $50. Each subsequent occurrence shall incur a $100 fine.
8.6.2. A team that fails to provide required information, or provides incorrect information, when requested by the Match Secretaries or Umpiring Committee shall be fined $50. This includes umpire details due by noon on the Thursday before the game. Each subsequent occurrence shall incur a $100 fine.
8.7. Improper attire:
8.7.1. A player who is not wearing the team uniform required by Section
3.7.1 shall be excluded from the match by either umpire or the opposing team. An excluded player does not count as present for the toss or start-of-play requirements, including the minimum of seven players. The umpires or opposing team must submit photographic or video evidence to the Match Secretaries.
8.7.2. Captains should photograph the opposing team’s playing eleven together with the umpires and attach the photograph to the scorecard. Failure to upload it will incur the penalties for incomplete scorecard information in Section
8.6.1. The photograph should be taken during the innings break.
8.8. Penalties for slow Over-rate.
8.8.1. Minor Over Rate Offense (To be applied progressively)
8.8.1.1. First Offense: $50 fine (regardless of overs)
8.8.1.2. Second Offense: $50 fine (regardless of overs)
8.8.1.3. Third or subsequent Offense: $50 fine (regardless of overs) plus suspension of Captain for 1 game Page | 19

[Page 20]
NCCA Winter T20 Standing Rules (10/26/2026)
8.8.2. Serious Over Rate Offense
8.8.2.1. $50 fine (regardless of overs) plus suspension of Captain for 1 game
8.9. Fines and Invoices.
8.9.1. If the Association fails to inform a team about a fine within 60 days of the infraction, the fine is revoked.
8.9.2. All fines are payable within 30 days of the invoice date.
8.9.3. For each overdue fine, teams will be penalized five (5) points and the fine will be increased by 10% for each month it remains unpaid after the initial 30-day period.
8.9.4. Player eligibility complaints should be reported within 4 weeks of the infraction during the regular season. For infractions in the last 2 weeks of the regular season, complaints should be reported within one week. The Executive Committee may decide whether to investigate complaints received after these periods.
8.10. Player No Shows at Games.
8.10.1. If no member of a home or visiting team arrives by game time and the team has not notified the umpires, Match Secretaries and opposing captain in advance, the offending team shall be fined $200 and receive a 10-point penalty, in addition to other applicable penalties. For a postseason game, the fine shall be $300. 9. Awards Individual and Team Awards shall be given in each Season as per the following sections.

ICC MEN’S TWENTY20 INTERNATIONAL PLAYING CONDITIONS Effective from October 2026

[Page 2]
PREAMBLE – THE SPIRIT OF CRICKET Cricket owes much of its appeal and enjoyment to the fact that it should be played not only according to the Laws (which are incorporated within these Playing Conditions), but also within the Spirit of Cricket. The major responsibility for ensuring fair play rests with the captains, but extends to all players, match officials and, especially in junior cricket, teachers, coaches and parents. Respect is central to the Spirit of Cricket. Respect your captain, team-mates, opponents and the authority of the umpires. Play hard and play fair. Accept the umpire’s decision. Create a positive atmosphere by your own conduct, and encourage others to do likewise. Show self-discipline, even when things go against you. Congratulate the opposition on their successes, and enjoy those of your own team. Thank the officials and your opposition at the end of the match, whatever the result. Cricket is an exciting game that encourages leadership, friendship and teamwork, which brings together people from different nationalities, cultures and religions, especially when played within the Spirit of Cricket. 1 THE PLAYERS
1.1 Number of players A match is played between two sides, each of 11 players, one of whom shall be captain.
1.2 Nomination and replacement of players
1.2.1 Each captain shall nominate 11 players plus a maximum of four (4) substitute fielders in writing to the ICC Match Referee before the toss. Other than as set out in clause 1.2.7, no player (member of the playing 11) may be changed after the nomination and prior to the start of play without the consent of the opposing captain.
1.2.2 Only those nominated as substitute fielders shall be entitled to act as substitute fielders during the match, unless the ICC Match Referee, in exceptional circumstances, allows subsequent additions.
1.2.3 All those nominated including those nominated as substitute fielders, as well as any Concussion Replacements, must be eligible to play for that particular team and by such nomination the nominees shall warrant that they are so eligible.
1.2.4 In addition, by their nomination, the nominees shall be deemed to have agreed to abide by all the applicable ICC Regulations pertaining to international cricket and in particular, the Clothing and Equipment Regulations, the Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel (hereafter referred to as the ICC Code of Conduct), the Anti-Discrimination Code for Players and Player Support Personnel, the Anti-Doping Code and the Anti-Corruption Code.
1.2.5 A player or player support personnel who has been suspended from participating in a match shall not, from the toss of the coin and for the remainder of the match thereafter:
1.2.5.1 Be nominated as, or carry out any of the duties or responsibilities of a substitute fielder, or
1.2.5.2 Enter any part of the playing area (which shall include the field of play and the area between the boundary and the perimeter boards) at any time, including any scheduled or unscheduled breaks in play.
1.2.6 A player who has been suspended from participating in a match shall be permitted from the toss of the coin and for the remainder of the match thereafter be permitted to enter the players’ dressing room provided that the players’ dressing room (or any part thereof) for the match is not within the playing area described in clause
1.2.5.2 above (for example, the player is not permitted to enter the on-field ‘dugout’).
1.2.7 Concussion Replacement
1.2.7.1 If a player sustains a concussion or suspected concussion as a result of a head or neck injury during the course of the relevant match, a Concussion Replacement may be permitted in the following circumstances:
1.2.7.1.1 the head or neck injury must have been sustained during play and within the playing area described in clause
1.2.5.2 above;
1.2.7.1.2 a concussion or suspected concussion must have been formally diagnosed by the Team Medical Representative;
1.2.7.1.3 the Team Medical Representative or Team Manager shall submit a Concussion Replacement Request to the ICC Match Referee on a standard form, which shall:
1.2.7.1.3.1 identify the player who has sustained the concussion or suspected concussion;
1.2.7.1.3.2 specify the incident in which the concussion or suspected concussion was sustained, including the time at which it occurred; ICC MEN'S TWENTY20 INTERNATIONAL PLAYING CONDITIONS 4

[Page 5]
1.2.7.1.3.3 confirm that, following an examination, the Team Medical Representative believes or suspects that the player has sustained a concussion as a result of the incident specified in clause
1.2.7.1.3.2 above; and
1.2.7.1.3.4 identify the requested Concussion Replacement from the list of nominated concussion replacements submitted for the match, who shall be a like-for-like replacement for the player who has sustained the concussion or suspected concussion. Under exceptional circumstances, the ICC Match Referee will consider a request for a replacement player outside of the nominated concussion replacement players for the match. In such circumstances the ICC Match Referee shall apply the provisions of clauses 1.2.7.3,
1.2.7.4 and
1.2.7.5.
1.2.7.2 The Concussion Replacement Request must be submitted as soon as possible after the incident specified in clause
1.2.7.1.3.2 if a Concussion Replacement is to be permitted.
1.2.7.3 The ICC Match Referee should ordinarily approve a Concussion Replacement Request if the replacement is a like-for-like player whose inclusion will not excessively advantage his team for the remainder of the match.
1.2.7.4 In assessing whether the nominated Concussion Replacement should be considered a like-for-like player, the ICC Match Referee should consider the likely role the concussed player would have played during the remainder of the match, and the normal role that would be performed by the nominated Concussion Replacement.
1.2.7.5 If the ICC Match Referee believes that the inclusion of the nominated Concussion Replacement, when performing their normal role, would excessively advantage their team, the ICC Match Referee may impose such conditions upon the identity and involvement of the Concussion Replacement as they see fit, in line with the overriding objective of facilitating a like-for-like replacement for the concussed player. For clarity, a concussion replacement will inherit all warnings, penalty time and suspensions that were imposed on the replaced player.
1.2.7.6 The ICC Match Referee may, in reviewing a Concussion Replacement Request made in accordance with clause 1.2.7.1.3, request any such further information as may be required in order to make the determination required under clauses 1.2.7.1.1, 1.2.7.1.2,
1.2.7.4 and
1.2.7.5.
1.2.7.7 The decision of the ICC Match Referee in relation to any Concussion Replacement Request shall be final and neither team shall have any right of appeal.
1.2.7.8 Once the Concussion Replacement has been approved by the ICC Match Referee, the replaced player shall play no further part in the match.
1.2.7.9 Both the Concussion Replacement and the replaced player shall be considered to have played in the match for records and statistical purposes.
1.3 Captain
1.3.1 If at any time the captain is not available, a deputy shall act for him.
1.3.2 If a captain is not available to nominate the players, then any person associated with that team may act as his deputy to do so. See clause
1.2.
1.3.3 At any time after the nomination of the players, only a nominated player can act as deputy in discharging the duties and responsibilities of the captain as stated in these Playing Conditions, including at the toss. See clause
13.4 (The toss). ICC MEN'S TWENTY20 INTERNATIONAL PLAYING CONDITIONS 5

[Page 6]
1.4 Responsibility of captains The captains are responsible at all times for ensuring that play is conducted within the Spirit of Cricket as well as within these Playing Conditions. 2 THE UMPIRES
2.1 Appointment and attendance The following rules for the selection and appointment of T20I umpires shall be followed as far as it is practicable to do so:
2.1.1 The umpires shall control the game as required by these Playing Conditions, with absolute impartiality, and shall be present at the ground at least two hours before the scheduled start of play.
2.1.2 The following Match Officials are to be appointed for each T20I match:
2.1.2.1 One (1) ICC Match Referee, appointed by the ICC from an ICC Panel of Match Referees.
2.1.2.2 Two (2) on-field umpires, appointed by the Home Board from their representatives on an ICC Panel of Umpires.
2.1.2.3 One (1) third umpire, appointed by the Home Board from their representatives on an ICC Panel of Umpires, who shall act as the emergency on-field umpire. The DRS Protocol governing the use of DRS and the third umpire is set out in Appendix D.
2.1.2.4 One (1) fourth umpire, appointed by the Home Board from its panel of first-class umpires. The fourth umpire shall act as the emergency third umpire. In ‘DRS’ T20I matches, the fourth umpire shall be appointed by the Home Board from their representatives on an ICC Panel of Umpires.
2.1.3 Neither team shall have a right of objection to the appointment of any umpire or ICC Match Referee.
2.2 Change of umpire An umpire shall not be changed during the match, other than in exceptional circumstances, unless they are injured or ill.
2.3 Consultation with Home Board Before the match the umpires shall consult with the Home Board to determine:
2.3.1 the balls to be used during the match. See clause 4 (The ball).
2.3.2 the hours of play and the times and durations of any agreed intervals.
2.3.3 which clock or watch and back-up time piece is to be used during the match.
2.3.4 the boundary of the field of play. See clause 19 (Boundaries).
2.3.5 the use of covers. See clause 10 (Covering the pitch).
2.3.6 any special conditions of play affecting the conduct of the match. inform the scorers of agreements in 2.3.2, 2.3.3,
2.3.4 and
2.3.6.
2.4 The wickets, creases and boundaries Before the toss and during the match, the umpires shall satisfy themselves that
2.4.1 the creases are correctly marked. See clause 7 (The creases).
2.4.2 the wickets are properly positioned. See clause 8 (The wickets).
2.4.3 the boundary of the field of play complies with the requirements of clauses
19.1 (Determining the boundary of the field of play),
19.2 (Identifying and marking the boundary) and
19.3 (Restoring the boundary). ICC MEN'S TWENTY20 INTERNATIONAL PLAYING CONDITIONS 6

[Page 7]
2.5 Conduct of the match, implements and equipment Before the toss and during the match, the umpires shall satisfy themselves that
2.5.1 the conduct of the match is strictly in accordance with these Playing Conditions.
2.5.2 the implements used in the match conform to the following
2.5.2.1 clause 4 (The ball).
2.5.2.2 externally visible requirements of clause 5 (The bat) and paragraph 1 of Appendix B.
2.5.2.3 either clauses
8.2 (Size of stumps) or
8.3 (The bails).
2.5.3 no player uses equipment other than that permitted. See paragraph 2 of Appendix A. Note particularly therein the interpretation of ‘protective helmet’.
2.5.4 the wicket-keeper’s gloves comply with the requirements of clause
27.2 (Gloves).
2.6 Fair and unfair play The umpires shall be the sole judges of fair and unfair play.
2.7 Fitness for play
2.7.1 It is solely for the umpires together to decide whether either conditions of ground, weather or light or exceptional circumstances mean that it would be dangerous or unreasonable for play to take place. Conditions shall not be regarded as either dangerous or unreasonable merely because they are not ideal. The fact that the grass and the ball are wet does not warrant the ground conditions being regarded as unreasonable or dangerous.
2.7.2 Conditions shall be regarded as dangerous if there is actual and foreseeable risk to the safety of any player or umpire.
2.7.3 Conditions shall be regarded as unreasonable if, although posing no risk to safety, it would not be sensible for play to proceed.
2.7.4 If the umpires consider the ground is so wet or slippery as to deprive – the bowler of a reasonable foothold – the fielders of the ability to move freely – the batters of the ability to play their strokes or to run between the wickets then these conditions shall be regarded as so bad that it would be dangerous and unreasonable for play to take place.
2.8 Suspension of play in dangerous or unreasonable circumstances
2.8.1 All references to ground include the pitch. See clause
6.1 (Area of pitch).
2.8.2 If at any time the umpires together agree that the conditions of ground, weather or light, or any other circumstances are dangerous or unreasonable, they shall immediately suspend play, or not allow play to start or to recommence. The decision as to whether conditions are so bad as to warrant such action is one for the umpires alone to make, following consultation with the ICC Match Referee.
2.8.3 If circumstances are warranted, the umpires shall stop play and instruct the Ground Authority to take whatever action they can and use whatever equipment is necessary to remove as much dew as possible from the outfield when conditions become unreasonable or dangerous. The umpires may also instruct the ground staff to take such action during scheduled and unscheduled breaks in play.
2.8.4 The umpires shall disregard any shadow on the pitch from the stadium or from any permanent object on the ground.
2.8.5 Light Meters It is the responsibility of the ICC to supply light meters to the match officials to be used in accordance with these Playing Conditions.
2.8.5.1 All light meters shall be uniformly calibrated. ICC MEN'S TWENTY20 INTERNATIONAL PLAYING CONDITIONS 7

2.8.5.3.2 As benchmarks for the remainder of a match.
2.8.6 Use of artificial lights If in the opinion of the umpires, natural light is deteriorating to an unfit level, they shall authorise the Ground Authority to use the available artificial lighting so that the match can commence or continue in acceptable conditions. 2.8.7 When there is a suspension of play it is the responsibility of the umpires to monitor conditions. They shall make inspections as often as appropriate, unaccompanied by any players or officials. 2.8.8 The safety of all persons within the ground is of paramount importance to the ICC. In the event of any threatening circumstance, whether actual or perceived (including for example weather, pitch invasions, act of God, etc.), then the umpires, on the advice of the ICC Match Referee, should suspend play and all players and officials should immediately be asked to leave the field of play in a safe and orderly manner and to relocate to a secure and safe area (depending on each particular threat) pending the satisfactory passing or resolution of such threat or risk to the reasonable satisfaction of the umpires, the ICC Match Referee, the head of the relevant Ground Authority, the head of ground security and/or the police as the circumstances may require.

2.9 Position of umpires The umpires shall stand where they can best see any act upon which their decision may be required. 2.13 Signals
2.13.1 The following code of signals shall be used by umpires.
2.13.1.1 Signals made while the ball is in play No ball – by extending one arm horizontally. Out – by raising an index finger above the head. (If Not out, the umpire shall call Not out.) Wide – by extending both arms horizontally. Dead ball – by crossing and re-crossing the wrists below the waist.
2.13.1.2 When the ball is dead, the bowler’s end umpire shall repeat the signals in clause 2.13.1.1, with the exception of the signal for Out, to the scorers.
2.13.1.3 The signals listed below shall be made to the scorers only when the ball is dead. Boundary 4 – by waving an arm from side to side finishing with the arm across the chest. Boundary 6 – by raising both arms above the head. Bye – by raising an open hand above the head. Five Penalty runs awarded to the batting side – by repeated tapping of one shoulder with the opposite hand. Five Penalty runs awarded to the fielding side – by placing one hand on the opposite shoulder. Leg bye – by touching a raised knee with the hand. Revoke last signal – by touching both shoulders, each with the opposite hand. Short run – by bending one arm upwards and touching the nearer shoulder with the tips of the fingers. Free Hit – after signalling the No ball, the bowler’s end umpire extends one arm straight upwards and moves it in a circular motion. Powerplay Over – by rotating their arm in a large circle. The following signal is for Level 4 player conduct offences. The signal has two parts, both of which should be acknowledged separately by the scorers. Level 4 conduct Part 1 – by putting one arm out to the side of the body and repeatedly raising it and lowering it. Part 2 – by raising an index finger, held at shoulder height, to the side of the body.
2.13.1.4 All the signals in clause
2.13.1.3 are to be made by the bowler’s end umpire except that for Short run, which is to be signalled by the umpire at the end where short running occurs. However, the bowler’s end umpire shall be responsible both for the final signal of Short run to the scorers and, if more than one run is short, for informing them as to the number of runs to be recorded.
2.13.2 The umpire shall wait until each signal to the scorers has been separately acknowledged by a scorer before allowing play to proceed.
2.13.2.1 If several signals are to be used, they should be given in the order that the events occurred.
2.13.2.2 Where more than one contravention of these Playing Conditions occurs during the same delivery, any sanctions under each clause shall be applied independently, unless otherwise stated. 6 THE PITCH
6.1 Area of pitch The pitch is a rectangular area of the ground 22 yards/20.12 metres in length and 10 feet/3.05 metres in width. It is bounded at either end by the bowling creases and on either side by imaginary lines, one each side of the imaginary line joining the centres of the two middle stumps, each parallel to it and 5 feet/1.52 metres from it. If the pitch is next to an artificial pitch which is closer than 5 feet/1.52 metres from the middle stumps, the pitch on that side will extend only to the junction of the two surfaces. See clauses
8.1 (Description, width and position),
7.2 (The bowling crease) and Appendix C.
6.2 Fitness of pitch for play The umpires shall be the sole judges of the fitness of the pitch for play. See clauses
2.7 (Fitness for play) and
2.8 (Suspension of play in dangerous or unreasonable conditions).
6.3 Selection and preparation Before the match, the Ground Authority shall be responsible for the selection and preparation of the pitch. During the match, the umpires shall control its use and maintenance.
6.3.1 The Ground Authority shall ensure that during the period prior to the start of play and during intervals, the pitch area shall be roped off so as to prevent unauthorised access. (The pitch area shall include an area at least 2 metres either side of the playing pitch and behind the bowling crease at each end of the pitch.)
6.3.2 The fourth umpire shall ensure that, prior to the start of play and during any intervals, only authorised staff, the ICC match officials, players, team coaches and authorised television personnel shall be allowed access to the pitch area. Such access shall be subject to the following limitations:
6.3.2.1 Only captains and team coaches may walk on the actual playing surface of the pitch area (outside of the crease markings).
6.3.2.2 Access to the pitch area by television personnel shall be restricted to one camera crew (including one or two television commentators) of the official licensed television broadcaster(s) (but not news crews).
6.3.2.3 No spiked footwear shall be permitted.
6.3.2.4 No one shall be permitted to bounce a ball on the pitch, strike it with a bat or cause damage to the pitch in any other way.
6.3.2.5 Access shall not interfere with pitch preparation.
6.3.3 In the event of any dispute, the ICC Match Referee will rule and their ruling will be final.
6.4 Changing the pitch
6.4.1 If the on-field umpires decide that it is dangerous or unreasonable for play to continue on the match pitch, they shall stop play and immediately advise the ICC Match Referee.
6.4.2 The on-field umpires and the ICC Match Referee shall then consult with both captains.
6.4.3 If the captains agree to continue, play shall resume.
6.4.4 If the decision is not to resume play, the on-field umpires together with the ICC Match Referee shall consider whether the existing pitch can be repaired and the match resumed from the point it was stopped. In considering whether to authorise such repairs, the ICC Match Referee must consider whether this would place either side at an unfair advantage, given the play that had already taken place on the dangerous pitch.
6.4.5 If the decision is that the existing pitch cannot be repaired, then the match is to be abandoned with the following consequences:
6.4.5.1 In the event of the required number of overs to constitute a match having been completed at the time the match is abandoned, the result shall be determined according to the provisions of clause
16.4.2. ICC MEN'S TWENTY20 INTERNATIONAL PLAYING CONDITIONS 13

11 INTERVALS
11.1 An interval
11.1.1 The following shall be classed as intervals. – Intervals between innings. – A drinks interval. – Any other agreed interval.
11.1.2 Only these intervals shall be considered as scheduled breaks for the purposes of clause
24.2.6 (fielder absent or leaving the field of play).
11.2 Duration of interval
11.2.1 There shall be a 15-minute interval between innings, taken from the call of Time before the interval until the call of Play on resumption after the interval.
11.3 Allowance for interval between innings Law
11.3 of the Laws of Cricket shall not apply.
11.4 Changing agreed times of intervals
11.4.1 If the innings of the team batting first is completed prior to the scheduled time for the interval, the interval shall take place immediately and the innings of the team batting second will commence correspondingly earlier.
11.4.2 However, following a lengthy delay or interruption prior to the completion of the innings of the team batting first, the Match Referee may, at their discretion, reduce the interval between innings from 15 minutes to not less than 10 minutes.
11.4.3 Such discretion should only be exercised after determining the adjusted overs per side based on a 15-minute interval. If, having exercised this discretion, the rescheduled finishing time for the match is earlier than the latest possible finishing time, then these minutes should be deducted from the length of any interruption during the second innings before determining the overs remaining.
11.5 Intervals for drinks
11.5.1 Subject to the prior agreement between both participating Member Boards, one scheduled drinks interval of 2 minutes 30 seconds may be taken at the midpoint of each innings.
11.5.1.1 The following shall apply for the drinks break: – No practice is allowed. – If the scheduled number of overs in an interrupted match is 14 overs or less, there will be no drinks break. – Following a lengthy delay or interruption prior to the drinks break, the ICC Match Referee may, at their discretion, cancel all the remaining drinks breaks for the match. – The Head Coach or their designate may consult with the on-field players during the drinks break for tactical reasons.
11.5.2 An individual player may be given a drink either on the boundary edge or at the fall of a wicket, on the field, provided that no playing time is wasted. No other drinks shall be taken on to the field without the permission of the umpires. Any player taking drinks on to the field shall be dressed in proper cricket attire (subject to the wearing of bibs – refer to the note in clause 24.1.4).

12.1 Call of Play The bowler’s end umpire shall call Play before the first ball of the match and on the resumption of play after any interval or interruption.

12.7.1 To be determined by the Home Board subject to there being two sessions of 1 hour 25 minutes each, separated by a 15-minute interval between innings. 12.8.1 The minimum over rate to be achieved in T20I matches shall be

13.3.2 at the fall of a wicket or the retirement of a batter, further balls remain to be bowled but no further batter is available to come in.

13.6 Duration of match
13.6.1 All matches will consist of one innings per side, each innings being limited to a maximum of 20 overs. All matches shall be of one day’s scheduled duration provided that participating countries in a series may agree to provide for a reserve day on which an incomplete match may be replayed or continued from the scheduled day.
13.6.2 If the match is to be continued on the reserve day, every effort shall be made to complete the match on the scheduled day with any necessary reduction in overs taking place and only if the minimum number of overs necessary to constitute a match cannot be bowled on the scheduled day will the match be completed on the reserve day.
13.6.3 If the match has started on the scheduled day and overs are subsequently reduced following an interruption, but no further play is possible, the match will resume on the reserve day under the same assumption that the last ball was played on the scheduled day. Refer to Appendix G.
13.7 Length of innings
13.7.1 Uninterrupted matches.
13.7.1.1 Each team shall bat for 20 overs unless all out earlier.
13.7.1.2 If the team fielding first fails to bowl the required number of overs by the scheduled time for cessation of the first innings, play shall continue until the required number of overs has been bowled. The team batting second shall receive its full quota of 20 overs irrespective of the number of overs it bowled in the scheduled time for the cessation of the first innings.
13.7.1.3 If the team batting first is dismissed in less than 20 overs, the team batting second shall be entitled to bat for 20 overs.
13.7.1.4 If the team fielding second fails to bowl 20 overs by the scheduled cessation time, the hours of play shall be extended until the required number of overs has been bowled or a result is achieved.
13.7.1.5 Penalties shall apply for slow over rates (refer to clause
13.8 and the ICC Code of Conduct).
13.7.2 Delayed or interrupted matches
13.7.2.1 Delay or Interruption to the Innings of the Team Batting First (see paragraph 1 of Appendix E)
13.7.2.1.1 When playing time has been lost the revised number of overs to be bowled in the match shall be based on a rate of
14.11 overs per hour in the total remaining time available for play.
13.7.2.1.2 The revision of the number of overs should ensure, whenever possible, that both teams have the opportunity of batting for the same number of overs. The team batting second shall not bat for a greater number of overs than the first team unless the latter completed its innings in less than its allocated overs. To constitute a match, a minimum of five (5) overs have to be bowled to the side batting second, subject to a result not being achieved earlier.
13.7.2.1.3 As soon as the total minutes of playing time remaining is less than the completed overs faced by Team 1 multiplied by 4.25, then the first innings is terminated and the provisions of
13.7.2.2 below take effect.
13.7.2.1.4 A fixed time will be specified for the commencement of the interval, and also the close of play for the match, by applying a rate of
14.11 overs per hour. When calculating the length of playing time available for the match, or the length of either innings, the timing and duration of all relative delays, extensions in playing hours, interruptions in play, and intervals will be taken into consideration. 13.7.2.1.5 If the team fielding first fails to bowl the revised number of overs by the specified time, play shall continue until the required number of overs have been bowled or the innings is completed.

13.7.3 Extra Time The participating countries may agree to provide for extra time where the start of play is delayed or play is suspended. 13.8 Over-rate penalties
13.8.1 The fielding side shall be in position to bowl the first ball of the final over of the innings by the scheduled (or re-scheduled) cessation time for the innings (calculated in accordance with clause 13.7). 13.9.1 No bowler shall bowl more than four (4) overs in an innings.

13.9.3 For innings of rescheduled length of between five (5) and nine (9) overs, no bowler may bowl more than two overs.
13.9.4 In the event of a bowler breaking down and being unable to complete an over, the remaining balls will be allowed by another bowler. Such part of an over will count as a full over only in so far as each bowler’s limit is concerned.

16 THE RESULT
16.1 A Win
16.1.1 Unless the winner is determined by DLS (see clause
16.4 – Calculation of the Target Score), the side which has scored in its one innings a total of runs in excess of that scored by the opposing side in its one completed innings shall win the match. See clause
13.3 (Completed innings). Note also clause
16.5 (Winning hit or extras).
16.1.2 Save for circumstances where a match is awarded to a team as a consequence of the opposing team’s refusal to play (clause 16.2), a result can be achieved only if both teams have had the opportunity of batting for at least five (5) overs, unless one team has been all out in less than five (5) overs or unless the team batting second scores enough runs to win in less than five (5) overs.
16.1.3 Save for circumstances where a match is awarded to a team as a consequence of the opposing team’s refusal to play (clause 16.2), all matches in which both teams have not had an opportunity of batting for a minimum of five (5) overs, shall be declared a No Result.
16.2 ICC Match Referee awarding a match
16.2.1 A match shall be lost by a side which either
16.2.1.1 concedes defeat or
16.2.1.2 in the opinion of the ICC Match Referee refuses to play and the ICC Match Referee shall award the match to the other side.
16.2.2 If an umpire considers that an action by any player or players might constitute a refusal by either side to play then the umpire shall call time, and the umpires together shall inform the ICC Match Referee of this fact. The ICC Match Referee shall together with the umpires ascertain the cause of the action. If the ICC Match Referee, after due consultation with the umpires, then decides that this action does constitute a refusal to play by one side, they shall so inform the captain of that side. If the captain persists in the action the ICC Match Referee shall award the match in accordance with clause
16.2.1.2 above.
16.2.3 If action as in clause
16.2.2 above takes place after play has started and does not constitute a refusal to play the delay or interruption in play shall be dealt with in the same manner as provided for in clauses
13.7.2 (Delayed and Interrupted Matches) and
11.4 (Changing agreed times for intervals) above. Note: In addition to the consequences of any refusal to play prescribed under this clause, any such refusal, whether temporary or final, may result in disciplinary action being taken against the captain and team responsible under the ICC Code of Conduct.
16.3 All other matches – A Tie or No Result
16.3.1 A Tie
16.3.1.1 If the teams’ scores are equal after both innings have been completed (if applicable under DLS – see clause 16.4), then a Super Over shall be played. If the Super Over is a tie, then unless exceptional circumstances arise (see paragraph 25 of Appendix F) subsequent Super Overs shall be played until there is a winner. Should it not be possible to play or to complete the Super Overs needed to determine a winner, the match shall be tied.
16.3.2 No Result See clause
16.1.3 above. ICC MEN'S TWENTY20 INTERNATIONAL PLAYING CONDITIONS 24
